not_mined: Heptaplus dedication/first proem details on Pythagorean and Egyptian lore (l. 3540-3600) beyond the method claims; only what bears on hidden meaning and Dionysius was taken.
First Exposition ch. 3-6 (l. 4402-4553) on the sublunary divisions, phenomena, Ennius, plants and animals: physical detail with no angelology; only ch. 1-3, 7 taken.
Second Exposition ch. 3-5 (l. 4794-4956) on planets, astral influence, Avicenna, constellations: astronomy; only the Hebrew-mystery claim taken.

Fourth Exposition ch. 1, 3-7 (l. 5548-5860) on body, spirit, senses, appetites, Manichaeans, Adam: moral psychology with no angelic content beyond the claims taken (fellowship with angels, illuminating intellect, active-intellect controversy).
Fifth Exposition ch. 3, 4 (astrology), ch. 6-7 partly: sea limits, Epicurus, Strato, Melito, prose on penalties.
Sixth Exposition ch. 2-5 (l. 6393-6552): the fifteen kinds of affinity in detail, prayer and pagan testimonies (Iamblichus, Porphyry).

Seventh Exposition ch. 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 (l. 6990-7560): the Jewish and gentile waters, the six millennia argument, Elijah's oracle, Talmud arithmetic, the fish, birds and beasts allegory, the firmament as law, baptism. Only claims on method, Hebrew sources, angels and demons were taken.
The Hebrew letter list of Beresit in the final exposition (l. 7642-7662) is OCR-garbled and was not quoted; the translations of its twelve words were quoted (l. 7665-7673).
Back-cover publisher blurb (l. 7740-7752) and copyright material are not Heptaplus text and were left out. It is publisher copy, not a scholar's claim.
Translators' notes on Biblical references, biographical dates, Numenius, Melito, Theodorus, the stone of Hercules and the Douay verse numbers were not taken: no bearing on angels, worlds or method.

proposed_topics.label: The Heptaplus's use of Hebrew authorities and the letter-permutation reading of the first word (Exposition of the First Phrase, Third Exposition proem, Seventh Exposition ch. 4); Pico's own hedging of the method
The composition of angels: number and unity, essence and being, act and potency (Third Exposition ch. 1; Fifth Exposition ch. 1)
Evil angels and demons: no difference of nature from the good angels; hangmen and lictors; Lucifer's ascent; demons of the air (Fourth-Seventh Expositions)

notes: PACKET COVERS the Heptaplus only (Carmichael's translation, work wallis1965, l. 3497 first proem to l. 7739). All claims are primary_text (Pico speaking through the translation). TRANSLATORS' NOTES: after the coordinator relaxed scholar_from_edition to a warning, 21 translators' notes are in the packet as scholar_claim claims (claimant 'the translators', per the Note on the Text, l. 1106-1107, which says the translators identified references from Garin; the front matter does not name who wrote which note). Each claim's pico_locus.ref names the note (e.g. 'translators' note 2 to Third Exposition proem'). They cover Dionysian source references (Caelestis hierarchia II, IV, VII, XI; Aquinas ST I q.89 a.1), Hierotheus as fictitious, Averroes De animae beatitudine, Simplicius Physica 27.2 for containment, Zohar cross-references (I 16a, I 25a), identifications of Isaac, Simeon, Samuel ben Hophni, Alfarabi, Ibn Tufail, and notes that Pico gives no source for two sayings. Expect claimant_mismatch and scholar_from_edition warnings. Footnotes are self-contained, so no OCR splice needed [...] marks. CRUXES: (1) The first four expositions are announced in the second proem in the order angelic, celestial, sublunary, human, but the work gives elemental first, celestial second, angelic third (contents at l. 133-138; proem l. 4038-4045). (2) The second proem calls man 'a fourth world'; Fifth Exposition ch. 6 says man is 'not so much a fourth world' as their bond; the first-phrase exposition speaks again of 'the four worlds'. (3) 'Heaven' and 'earth' change referent from exposition to exposition (act/potency, being/essence, angels/men) as the second proem announces. (4) Third Exposition ch. 3 counts the contemplative hierarchy first, ch. 5 calls it the third. Only the third hierarchy's orders (principalities, archangels, angels) are named there; seraphim appear in ch. 6 as Isaiah's winged Seraphim, cherubim in the second proem and thrones only in Second Exposition ch. 1 (Isaac reading Ezekiel's sapphire throne as the tenth sphere). No scheme of seven interpretive layers appears; the seven are the seven expositions, each in seven chapters with the seventh turned to Christ. VERIFIED against the earlier audit: the Third Exposition is l. 5069-5488; Pico says he could expound Moses by both the Hebrew and the Dionysian teaching (l. 5085-5088), postpones the Hebrew (l. 5088-5099), treads in the footsteps of Dionysius 'or rather Paul and Hierotheus' (l. 5111-5112), and treats angels by number and unity 'after the Pythagorean custom' (l. 5132). The Kabbalistic exposition of the first phrase starts at l. 7568 as the audit said. OCR: footnote numerals run into the text and break many quotations across page marks; quotes were split or cut to avoid them (e.g. 'SyrianS' at l. 4765 is quoted as printed). Ficino: Pico calls him 'our friend Marsilio Ficino' and looks forward to his Latin Plotinus (l. 6127). Poliziano: a constant visitor at Fiesole (l. 3822-3825).
